messages:
maria-support: FYI Customer (AcmePayments) reports streaming API keeps dropping mid-response, client reconnects, then they see duplicate billing and partial messages. They have a pcap.
ryan-sre: Can you paste an example log or attach the pcap? We should check if connection is closed by the edge or client.
sophie-support: Uploading the short pcap snippet and the high-level repro steps from the customer. They say it often happens after ~8-12s of idle between chunks.
maria-support: Repro steps they gave: 1) open SSE with Accept: text/event-stream, 2) send prompt -> server streams tokens, 3) stream stops mid-token, client reconnects with Resume-Token, 4) they get both the truncated token and resumed tail (duplicates). Using our hosted region eu-west-1.
jules-eng: Curious — are we seeing a connection reset (RST) from the edge or an application-level close? Any 100-continue or proxy idle timeouts in fronting LB?
alex-eng-runtime: I pulled trace id trace-0a1b2c3d from their session. Edge logs show a FIN from client IP: 34.89.123.12 around the time of truncation. But downstream app logs show no explicit Close, it simply stops sending tokens for ~200ms then nothing. Strange.
ryan-sre: If FIN is client-originated it could be unstable mobile network. But duplicate billing implies client is reconnecting and we are not deduping tokens when resume happens. Need to confirm resume token TTL and our resume acceptance logic.
sophie-support: Customer attached tcpdump snippet: 
```
12:34:10.123456 IP 34.89.123.12.54321 > edge.elb: Flags [P.], seq 1000:1350, ack 500, win 64240, length 350
12:34:18.234567 IP edge.elb > 34.89.123.12.54321: Flags [P.], seq 500:760, ack 1350, win 65535, length 260
12:34:18.335678 IP 34.89.123.12.54321 > edge.elb: Flags [R], seq 1350, ack 760, win 0
```
They see R after the server chunk.
maria-support: They also included the client console log: 
```
EventStream.onmessage token: "...hel"
socket.onerror: ECONNRESET
socket.open() with resume-token: rt_abc123
```
And after resume they see final tokens again starting at "hel" -> duplicate fragment.
jules-eng: Ok, two things: (1) why is client sending R immediately after receiving a chunk? Could be client library (mobile) forcibly reset during TLS renegotiation or backgrounding. (2) why do we accept resume that overlaps content? We need to check resume granularity: are tokens deduped by offset or by checksum?
alex-eng-runtime: Current resume logic: resume-token contains kvcache pointer + last-seen-seq. If client reconnects and sends last-seen-seq=N, we start streaming from N+1. If client had received a partial token but not committed seq increment, it might ask to resume at the previous seq and then re-receive the fragment. We also rely on idempotency for billing via final token commit event, but that commit is only emitted after full completion. So partial duplicates can inflate billing.
ryan-sre: We should snapshot metrics: can you grab SLOs around that time?
sophie-support: Pasted metrics (short): 
- streaming.conn_count: 412
- streaming.resume_attempts: 28
- streaming.resume_success_rate: 0.78
- streaming.partial_emit_rate: 0.014
- edge.tcp_retransmits: +12% over baseline
Customer spike at 2026-03-12T12:34:00Z aligns.
alex-eng-runtime: Also found trace spans showing a 150ms stall in token generator before a flush. Looks like generator backpressure + client jitter -> client issues R.
maria-support: Customer asks for a mitigation ASAP — they can't afford duplicates on billing-sensitive workloads.
jules-eng: Short-term mitigations: 1) recommend increasing client-side debounce/keepalive (send 1s heartbeat) to avoid orphaning? 2) On server side, we can change resume acceptance to require last-ack checksum match before resuming to dedupe overlapped fragments. Need eng approval.
ryan-sre: Also check proxy idle timeouts: ALB default 60s shouldn't matter, but any intermediate proxies or mobile PWAs might close earlier.
sophie-support: Customer already tried keepalive and saw slight improvement but still happens on flaky carriers. They prefer server-side fix.
alex-eng-runtime: Proposed patch: when accepting resume-token, require that client-supplied last-seen-offset's trailing fragment flag matches a server-side committed flag. If server sees that last-seen-offset points to a non-committed partial fragment, we will trim replay to the fragment boundary instead of re-emitting the same bytes. This prevents duplicate billing because billing only counts committed tokens.
maria-support: That sounds promising. Do we have an RFC or small PR?
jules-eng: I'll open a tiny design PR and link it. For immediate action, engage billing to ensure we credit duplicates for this customer proactively.

pcap-bot: pcap uploaded: s_98765-2162506789.pcap (stored to internal bucket).
ryan-sre: Next steps: 1) eng runtime to validate resume trim logic + tests, 2) add monitoring alert for streaming.partial_emit_rate > 0.01 per tenant, 3) support to collect more pcaps from affected customers. Assigning to jules-eng for PR and alex-eng-runtime for implementation.
alex-eng-runtime: On it. Will start with unit tests around resume semantics and an integration pcap replay to replicate duplicate billing locally.
maria-support: Thanks — keep me posted. I'll update the customer that we're working on a server-side fix and billing review.
jules-eng: Created PR draft: https://git.redwood.ai/p/runtimex/patches/1234 (WIP) — includes resume checksum check + trimming logic.
sophie-support: Great. Marking this thread for follow-up after PR lands. :white_check_mark:
